newsitem.title: GERMANY: German court convicts pyramid investment leader.
newsitem.headline: German court convicts pyramid investment leader.

text.p: A Frankfurt court on Thursday convicted the ringleader of a so-called "pyramid" investment club of fraud and sentenced the woman to eight years in prison.

Damara Bertges, the president of the European Kings Club, was found guilty of heading an organisation that cheated 94,000 participants out of a total of 850 million marks ($560 million) over four years with a scheme promising staggering annual returns of as much as 72 percent.

The Kings Club collapsed in late 1995. Pyramid schemes rely on existing investors recruiting new members to finance these yields with their initial outlay. The schemes inevitably fail when not enough new recruits can be found to pay the returns of those higher up the pyramid.
Investors had to pay 1,400 marks to join the club, an outlay which was intended to guarantee them large payouts starting with 2,400 marks in the first year.
The court, which had already sentenced three other leaders of the club to long jail terms, said Bertges would intially be released from jail for about two months before the start of her sentence.
She has already spent two years in investigative custody.
The leaders were originally charged in connection with 33,000 cases of fraud linked to 675,000 illegal bank transactions. Of these, prosecutors selected 678 model cases for the trial.
